newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil's High Island 140 output rising.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil's High Island 140 output rising.

text.p: Pennzoil Co said Wednesday daily natural gas production at the High Island 140 field is expected to increase to about 50 million cubic feet in late January, an increase of 150 percent above current production volumes of 20 million cubic feet.

In addition, the company said, daily condensate production will increase to 400 barrels from 100 barrels as a result of two development wells. Production is from Miocene age reservoirs between 6,000 and 10,000 feet.
High Island 140 is in the Gulf of Mexico about 20 miles offshore Texas in 50 feet of water.
Pennzoil has a 100 percent working interest in the field, acquired in 1992 from Chevron Corp.

"By combining the multi-disciplinary talents of our Gulf of Mexico exploitation team with 3D seismic technology, we were able to see upside potential in this mature field," said Michael A. Osborne, Pepco's senior vice president for production operations.
"The first development well encountered 75 feet net of pay in two horizons," said Osborne. The well is currently flowing at a rate of 300 barrels of condensate per day.
The second development well encountered 300 feet of net pay in the main producing horizons in the field and is expected to produce about 30 million cubic feet daily.
